rhyme_aside: None for the name. The lowland children skip to that, and never notice they're counting. ...None for you either. Not yet. The cards will lend you one. They only ever lend.
That's the old count. Thread, frame, filling, and a gap where the name goes. You came up out of the Red with the first three. The gap is what we're here for.

crown_say.ossumancer: Turned up on its own. Oss-Vharoth, the frame that would not lie down when everything else did. It's had a hand on your spine since the pool. Bone holds you up now. Bone keeps count of you.
crown_say.hemomancer: Already face up, and warm. Nol-Shogthuth, the Mother of the Wheel, the flesh that keeps on growing with no mind to tell it stop. She's drinking already. She drinks what spills.
crown_say.animancer: There, at the crown. Yh'Anuul, behind her veil, at her loom. She's drawn one thread up out of the Red and she's holding it to the light. That's you. Don't wriggle.
crown_say.miasmancer: The Myriad. Not one, a crowd, riding the last breath out of the world, every one of them sick. You breathed in, coming up the stair. They came in with it.
crown_say.monk: The crown is... ah. That one. I won't say its name. It hasn't got one, and lending it one would be rude. A gap at the top of you where something ought to sit. Smiling, if a gap can.

deck_open: The deck. Every face anyone ever wore is in it, and some nobody has worn yet. Watch my hands. No, don't. Watch the cards. They're the ones doing it.
Old deck. Warm. It has read everyone who came up out of that pool, and it remembers the shape of their hands. It shuffles itself, really. I only hold it still.

set: First the brow. The face. Not the one you came up with, that's only the Red's. The one the Hide will know you by. Draw three, blind. Your hand knows more than your eyes do, tonight.
The brow, first. Every power keeps a deck of faces and lends them out like coats. Draw three. One of them has been waiting for your shape.

kin: {Brow} at the brow, and {a} in it again. The deck keeps handing you back to {crown}. It does that when it has made up its mind.
rev: A face that came up head down. Well. The world will meet you upside down, and you'll have to decide which of you is standing wrong.
default: So that's the face. {Brow_m}. Faces are cheap here, everyone's wearing someone's. What matters is what moves behind it.

set: Now the heart. Not the one that beats. The other one, under it, that wants. The deck likes that place best. It always finds something there.
The heart next. Lay your hand flat on the cloth there. Feel that? Warm. It's always warm there, whoever sits where you sit.

pair: Face and heart drawn from the same {asp}. No quarrel in you there. That's restful. It's also how a thing gets swallowed whole.
rev: The heart turned over. {Heart}, head down. Wanting backwards is still wanting. It's only harder to explain to anyone who asks.
default: {Brow_m}, over a heart that wants {heart_m}. Those two will argue all the way down the road. Let them. The arguing is where the walking comes from.

set: The left hand. The keeping hand, the shore folk say. Whatever closes in it you'll carry past all sense, and call it yours.
Left hand now. The one that holds on. What it closes on doesn't open easily, and doesn't open whole.

kin: {Lhand}, and the {a} in your keeping hand. {Crown} will feel that grip. It likes being held. It likes it a little too much.
rev: Reversed, in the keeping hand. You'll hold the wrong end of it. Everyone does, at first. Some never let go long enough to turn it round.
default: In the left, then, {lhand_m}. That's what you'll still be holding when the rest goes. Hold it loosely. Or don't, and see.

set: The right hand gives. It opens. What falls from it the Hide takes, and the Hide has never once given anything back.
Now the right. The hand that lets go. Every hand here is emptied in the end. This is only choosing the order.

both_rev: Both hands reversed. You'll grip what you ought to drop, and drop what you ought to grip. Clumsy. The clumsy last, sometimes. Nobody expects them to.
pair: Both hands out of the same {asp}. One keeps what the other lets go. That isn't a contradiction, here. That's a heartbeat.
default: Keeping {lhand_m}. Letting go of {rhand_m}. Between the two hands a life gets its shape, the way clay does between palms.

set: Down to the belly. Fear lives here, not in the head. The head only explains it afterward, and badly.
The belly. Where fear sits, low and warm, curled round itself. Draw gently. It wakes easily.

kin: Even the fear is {a}. {Crown} lives where you're afraid. Most powers do. It's the one door everybody leaves open.
rev: A fear upside down. {Belly}. Hold a fear like that to the light and it looks like a wish. Don't hold it to the light.
default: So. A face, a want, two hands, and down in the belly a fear of {belly_m}. It's starting to look like someone. Like everyone who ever came up those stairs.

set: Now the feet, and the road behind them. You came up a stair out of a pool, not long since. Never mind. Everyone gets a road. A road's a kindness.
The feet. Where you came from. You don't remember. Nobody does. The cards remember for you, and they remember generously.

many_rev: Look at it. Half of you lying head down. The Red reads things the other way up, so perhaps you're the right way round after all, and the rest of us are hanging.
kin: Even the road was {a}. The deck has been dealing you one thing again and again, in different coats. It isn't subtle. It has never had to be.
default: {Feet_m}. That's the road behind you. On top of it a fear, two hands, a heart, a face, and {crown} at the crown. Whole. Nearly.

set: One more. Not on the body. Under it, face down, in the Red. We don't turn that one. It turns us. Read. Red. Always red.

shapes.many_rev: Most of you came up head down. Don't fret. Everything here is the wrong way up. Ask the cities on the ridge.
shapes.none_rev: Not one card turned against you. I've seen that before. It didn't last.
shapes.heart_belly: You fear the very thing you want. That isn't a flaw. That's the shape of a pilgrim.
shapes.hands: Both hands out of the same suit. One of them will drop it, and you won't know which until it's on the ground.
shapes.calling: There's more {a} in you than you know. {Crown} is thorough.
shapes.under_rev: And the one in the Red lay head down too. Of course it did. It's the only card lying the right way.

close_sum: And this is what they made of you, all told.

open: Now. All of it at once, the way the cards meant it.
Listen, then. This is you, as the cards tell it. Not as you'd tell it. You'd lie.
feet: You came by {m}, though you'll swear you only climbed a stair.
The road first. {M}. You won't remember walking it. Roads here don't need you to.
brow: You rose out of the Red wearing {m}, and the Hide will know you by it.
And the face. {M}. Wear it well. It was worn before you.
heart: Behind the face, always, the wanting. {M}.
Under it all you want {m}. Quietly. Always.
belly: Low down, where nobody looks, you fear {m}. Keep the fear. It's the one thing here that won't lie to you.
And the fear, curled in the belly. {M}. Feed it nothing. It'll grow anyway.
lhand: The left hand keeps {m}, and opens for no one.
In the keeping hand, {m}. Mind the grip.
rhand: The right lets go of {m}, the way the tide lets go of the shore. Not for long.
And the right hand opens. {M}, gone. The Hide keeps what falls.
under: And the one in the Red, face down all this while. {N}. {s}
Last, the card under everything. {N}. {s}
close: That's the telling. It isn't finished. They never are.
That's you. For now. The cards are only ever for now.
tale.prophecy: The cards keep one last word back. It's for you, not for me.
go: The mirror, then, in the great face's mouth. Look into it until it looks back, and walk in. It's the only door this room has ever had.
Up the last step, into the black glass. Don't look back. Nothing behind you is yours anymore.

ossumancer: The bone has you. Feel it? You're standing straighter already. Ossuarch. Not a name. An office, and nobody has ever held it long.
Your mantle is black iron with bone grown through it. You'll keep the count now. Every bone out of its place will itch in you like a splinter you can't reach.
An Ossuarch lets things finish. Everything that was ever told is still dying, slowly, and someone has to say enough. The living will step aside for you. Not out of respect.
The cost is the bone itself. It grows under the plate, where nobody looks. You won't bend. One day you'll break, and someone else will put on the iron, and count you.
animancer: The thread pulled tight. Hollow Mystic. One of the circles that stopped covering the glass, and looked.
Your mantle is a coat of hollowed mirrors, and the dead stop at their own faces in every piece of it. People will turn their mirrors to the wall when you pass.
You'll keep the dead. Not save them. Keep them. The few left will hand you their dead anyway, because nobody else will hold them.
The cost is that they never go through. The loom never finishes, and you're a thread in it now, pulled tight. Hold still, little thread.
hemomancer: It was always going to come up red. Red Penitent. The processions will know your hat before they know your face.
Your mantle is the hood and the welts. You'll break the bloodletter's rule. Open yourself, call the Maiden down, and tell her what to make.
A Penitent tells a mindless thing what the blood is for. Someone forgot to tell it, once, and a wound hatched. Blood given is not blood taken. You'll say that often. You'll need to.
The cost is your own life, every time, and she drinks what spills. She'll leave you your mind. Mostly.
miasmancer: Breathe in. Shrine Keeper. The folk will say you steal breath. You'll say you still it. Both, and steel at the end of it.
Your mantle is the fan, and a cord at the wrist with a knot for every breath held. A cloud at your back will think other people's thoughts.
You'll hold what the wind is full of, grudges and lies and sour hopes, until it sets hard in the chest and comes out an edge.
The cost comes last. A keeper who holds too much walks down into the water, still holding. Not yet. Breathe out. Slowly.
monk: Nothing in the bowl. Of course. Empty Hand. A beggar of the Gilded Peak, or something wearing one.
Your mantle is gold so bright the face beneath it goes away. To be looked at and not seen. The Peak called that holy. The Peak isn't there anymore.
The gap at the top of you has two hands, both empty, and both unmake. One with light, one with dark. You're one of the hands now. Don't ask which.
The cost is that you keep nothing. Whatever you hold, you'll let go. Whatever you touch goes quiet. Put a name in the bowl. It won't keep.

mantles.one: the one who ends the turn
mantles.rev: the one who begins the next

brow: a blank face, which everyone will write on
They'll each see their own hand in it and call it yours. Let them. A face nobody can read is the oldest mask there is.
a face rubbed out and drawn again, and again
Something wore this face before you, and wiped it, and wore it. The page goes thin. One day the light will show through, and they'll see what's behind it.
heart: to be written at last, in anyone's hand
Wanting a story so badly you'd take a cruel one. Most do. The cruel ones are the ones that get finished.
to be left unwritten, just once
A want for the quiet between words. Careful. Something lives in that quiet, and it wants the same thing you do.
lhand: a clean page no one is let near
Kept back, kept for something. Nobody keeps a page that clean unless they know what's coming to write on it.
a page worn so thin the fire shows through
Every story ever tried on it, scraped off. Hold it to a lantern and you'll see them all, faint, and the last one isn't over.
rhand: every life you might have been
The hand opens and they all go, the might-have-beens, like ash off a palm. Lighter. Narrower. That's how a road gets made.
the one story you kept telling
You let go the tale you told about yourself. What's left has no story at all. A kind of freedom. A kind of drowning.
belly: passing through and leaving no mark
The Hide is full of the unmarked, and they don't rest well. You'll cut your sign into things. Walls. Faces. You'll call it remembering.
being written over in someone else's hand
The pen frightens you more than the blank. Sensible. Every face here was written by someone who wasn't wearing it.
feet: a road with no marks on it at all
No footprints ahead, none behind. Either nobody came this way, or everybody did and the sand forgave them.
a road walked so often it's only a ditch now
Worn a man deep by all who came before. You think you're the first. They all thought that, down in the ditch.
under: the turn nobody has taken yet
At the bottom of everything, blank, patient as a held breath. The deck keeps that one for the end of things. Odd to find it this early. Odd, or not early at all.
the first page of the next telling
Upside down, the blank is a beginning. Someone ends the turn so someone can start the next. I won't say who. The cards won't either.

turned.head: Blank, and still it found a way to lie upside down. Takes talent, that.
turned.hands: Nothing on it, nothing at all, and the empty thing came up inverted. Ending, that means. Or the start of something. Same card, turned.
turned.low: Down that low the Unwritten always lands on its head. The next turn starts underfoot. Mind where you step.

mantles.one: the one who walks and does not know why

brow: a hood, a staff, and nobody under them
The face of everyone on the road. People will look at you and see the last pilgrim they buried. Some will be kind for it. Some won't.
the face of one who sat down by the road
Tired before you've begun. A face like that gets left alone, mostly. Mostly is a long word on the Hide.
heart: to keep walking, and never ask where
The going is the want. Arriving would spoil it. A heart like that walks through anything, and anyone, to keep from stopping.
to sit down at last and not get up
You want the end of the road more than the road. Rest, you'll call it. The dead call it that too.
lhand: a staff worn smooth by someone else's grip
You hold what the last walker held. The staff knows the way better than the hand does. Let it lead, and wonder whose way it is.
a pair of boots you won't put back on
Holding on to the stopping. Clutching it. Some keep a grave like that, close and warm, and ready.
rhand: the reason you set out
You drop the why and keep the walking. You'll go a long way like that. You won't remember the point, and you'll be very good at it.
the road itself
You drop the road and the road doesn't notice. Roads never do. Someone else will be walking it by mourning.
belly: arriving
Afraid of the door at the end, because then you'd have to be someone. Better to be a pair of feet. Feet are never asked their name.
the road running out under you
That cold drop where the path stops and the dark doesn't. You'll dream of that edge. In the dream you'll walk toward it.
feet: the pilgrim trench, a man deep in the Hide
Feet past counting wore that road into the skin of the world. You came along it without walking it. That's how most of us came.
a road that ended in the middle of nowhere
You came from a place the road gave up on. Nothing's there now. Nothing has a way of following you.
under: a walker who never stopped
Under you another walks, step for step, upside down in the Red. It was walking before the stair. Don't look for it. It's looking for you.
one who stopped a long way back, and waits
Somewhere behind, a pilgrim sat down and never rose, and the road has been bending back toward them ever since. Toward you, then. Eventually.

turned.head: Look, the Pilgrim's sat down. On its head. Tired before the walk's begun.
turned.hands: There goes the walker, feet in the air. Stopped. I've seen that card stop in steadier hands than yours.
turned.low: Boots to the sky. So the road ends low, does it. Roads drain. They all drain somewhere.

mantles.one: the one who buries
mantles.rev: the one who digs them up

brow: a face kept clean of what the hands have done
The hands bury and the face never looks down. People will trust a face like that. You'll let them, and dig.
a face that looks into every grave it opens
You can't help looking. Every opened grave looks back a little, and leaves something in the eyes. You'll be known by that look.
heart: to put the past down deep and tamp it flat
A heart that wants things finished and covered. Neat rows. You'll make a fine keeper of the dead. A poor one of the living.
to know what was buried, and why
The want to open. Every faith here put something under on purpose. You'll want to see it. You will see it.
lhand: a grip that never once looks in
You keep the work and not the meaning. A hand like that can bury anything, a friend, a faith, itself, and sleep after.
a bone dug up and never put back
You carry what should be under, close against the body. It'll get heavier. Bones here always do, once someone starts counting them.
rhand: whatever you can't carry, into the ground
What you can't bear, you bury. That's mercy, nearly. The ground here keeps what it's given, and keeps count.
the order the dead were laid in
You let the rows go crooked. Somewhere the Matron feels a bone slip its place, and lifts her head.
belly: a grave that won't stay filled
The thing that climbs back. Wise to fear it. Nothing you bury here is quite as dead as it was told.
what comes up with the dirt
Not the dead. What the dead were buried with. Names, mostly. Names are worse.
feet: the long rows where the dead lie in their order
You walked out between the graves and the graves let you. They don't, usually. Something down there knew your step.
a churned road of opened graves
The way of the robbed and the risen. Your boots carry that dirt still. The dead will catch the smell of it and turn their heads.
under: everything you ever buried, lying very still
Under you, a field of quiet things, all put down by your own hands. You don't remember one of them. They remember you.
a grave dug open from below
Something under the Red has been digging upward, toward you. Patient work. It's close now. Put your ear to the floor sometime. Or don't.

turned.head: Hands digging upward, toward the face. Something buried is on its way up to meet you.
turned.hands: Working backwards, those Hands. Opening, not filling. Somebody's rest is about to be disturbed, and I have a feeling it's mine.
turned.low: The Gravedigger's turned over, down by the belly. What you put away long ago is coming back up the way it went in.

mantles.one: the one drawn to the light that burns it
mantles.wears: the moths with the pale faces

brow: a pale face turned always toward the fire
The moths wear faces like that, the old court's faces, flying at every lamp. You'll be mistaken for something holy. That's how the moths get close.
a face with the singe still on it
Burned once, and wearing the mark. People will know you've been near something bright. They'll wonder what you brought back from it.
heart: to reach the one light that will burn you
Knowing it will burn makes no difference. The burning is the want. Call it devotion, if the word helps.
nothing, now the burning's done
A cooled heart. Ash wants nothing. Ash is very hard to frighten, and very easy to scatter.
lhand: a veil held up to the flame
You keep the thin thing between yourself and the fire and call it protection. Look at it sideways and it's a wick.
a palm of ash that used to be a veil
You keep what's left of the burning, as proof. One breath and it's gone. You'll go very still near open doors.
rhand: your fear of the fire
You let go of the fear and keep the fire. Brave, the living call that. The moths call it the only way to fly.
the last of what the fire left
The hand opens on the ashes and the wind takes them. Nothing left to burn. Nothing left to be, for a while.
belly: the dark, more than the burning
Better to burn than be left unlit. A fear like that drives you toward the worst light there is, and gladly.
the pull of a light, again
Once burned, you fear the pull more than the pain. You'll feel it anyway. The pull doesn't ask.
feet: a road from lamp to lamp to lamp
You came the way the moths go, by the lights, never by the road between. Every lamp you passed is a little dimmer now.
a road through what had already burned
Cinder underfoot the whole way. You walked out of a fire that had finished. Someone else was the fuel.
under: a pull toward the brightest thing in the room
Under you something lifts its pale face to every light. One day the light will be yours, and it will come.
a scorch where something used to stand
Something burned here before you came up, and left its shape in the stone. Your height. Your stance. Fancy that.

turned.head: Dropped, like a moth that flew too close. The Veil's already singed, look at the edge of it.
turned.hands: The Singed Veil, scorched side up. Nothing left on it to burn. That's either peace, or the end of the line.
turned.low: Ash settles low. That's where the Veil fell, upside down. Everything settles, given long enough.

mantles.one: the one who is carried
mantles.rev: the knife that cut the cloth
mantles.wears: every child the Deep asks for

brow: a face wrapped tight against the ash
A face not yet shown to the world. Others will want to shield it, and will think shielding makes it theirs.
a face cut free of its wrappings
Raw to the air and too new for it. You'll be stared at. New things are, here, by things that remember being new.
heart: to be carried, and to carry
The weight and the arms, both at once. You'll pick up more than you can bear and call it love, and you'll be right.
the knife, and the cut it makes
To be free of the wrapping, whatever it costs the hands that wrapped you. Every child wants that. The Deep counts on it.
lhand: a bundle you won't set down even to sleep
Something small and warm, and you won't say what. Nobody asks. Don't you ask either.
a short knife, still sharp
Kept close, kept clean. A knife for cloth, you'll say. Cloth is the least of what a knife learns.
rhand: the arms that carried you
You set down the ones who held you, and walk. Someone's arms will ache a long while after. That's the price of being carried.
the cloth you were cut out of
The wrappings fall and you don't look back at them. Somewhere the Deep notes one fewer, and asks again.
belly: being set down and left
Older than the dark, that fear. You'll keep company you shouldn't, to keep from feeling it.
whatever was in the bundle
Afraid of what you carry, and still carrying it. Fear and love feel the same in the arms.
feet: a road you never walked, carried the whole way
Somebody bore you here step by step while you slept. Ask whose back. Don't expect an answer.
a road away from the Deep, at a run
Somebody cut the cloth and ran with you under one arm. Who's still running, I wonder. And who stopped.
under: a child the Deep asked for
Under you, wrapped and waiting, a little one meant for the dark. Were you the one given, or the one kept back? The card won't say. It never has.
the knife that answered the Deep
Someone refused the asking once, with a blade. The refusal is still down there in the Red, still sharp. It knows a name for you before you have one.

turned.head: Cut loose. The cloth's in ribbons and the Swaddling's on its head.
turned.hands: The knife side of the Swaddling. Somebody always holds the knife. Mostly it's the one who was wrapped.
turned.low: Bare to the cold, down there. The Swaddling unwrapped, head down. Somebody let you out early.

mantles.one: the one who ends
mantles.rev: the one who keeps it under

brow: the face the harvest sees last
A face for endings. The dying will be calm under it, or not. Either way they'll look at it longest of anything.
a counting face under a plate of bone
The keeper's face, the one that holds the end down. Stern. Tired. Patient. You'll look older than you are, very soon.
heart: the harvest, every stalk of it
A heart that wants things to finish. Not cruel. Tidy. Everything ripe should come down. That's the trouble with it.
one more day before the harvest
To hold the end back a little longer, and longer. Every day bought is a day owed. The Gleaner keeps a count of those too.
lhand: an edge that has never missed
The end of things, in one hand. That hand will be steady. It's the other that'll shake.
a sliver of the edge, set in your own plate
A splinter of the harvest, carried inside the armour, close to the skin. You'll ache at every death nearby, the way old men ache at weather.
rhand: whatever is ripe
You let the ripe things go to the edge without a fight. Merciful, or tired. The ripe can't tell the difference.
the count, for one moment
You loosen your grip on the count, once, and something below stirs. One moment. Old Scythe has never needed more than one.
belly: being the harvest
Everyone is a stalk in a field. It's only that you've seen the edge coming.
losing count
The keeper's fear. Lose the count and the pit opens. So you'll count, under your breath, always, even in sleep.
feet: the road Old Scythe walks up out of his pit
The reaper's road, walked once an age. It was warm when you came along it. That should worry anyone who knows the timing.
the narrow stair down to the pit
You came up the way the keepers go down. Against the traffic. The keepers will notice, and look at you sideways.
under: Old Scythe, waiting for his age to come round
Under everything, the end of everything, resting. It isn't a threat. It's a calendar.
someone below, counting, so he stays under
Down there a keeper counts without stopping, and the end stays down. If the counting ever stops... Listen. ...Still counting. Good.

turned.head: Not the reaper. The keeper. Old Scythe's card, inverted, and someone holding the end down by the hair.
turned.hands: Counting instead of cutting. That's how the Gleaner reads the other way up. Count with him. He likes company.
turned.low: Down at the pit, the Gleaner turned. That's where the keepers stand guard. Cold work, and nobody thanks you.

mantles.one: the one who suffers to be believed
mantles.rev: the crowd that came to watch

brow: a weeping face that everyone believes
Grief worn so well it becomes a kind of proof. People will follow that face. You'll have to keep weeping, or they'll stop.
a face lost in the crowd
One more watcher. Nobody looks twice. The safest place to stand, and the most damning.
heart: to be believed, whatever it costs
Wanting so badly to be true that you'll bleed for it. Blood is how you're believed here. Ask the girl in the iron.
to watch, and be no part of it
To stand near suffering and feel the heat of it, safe. A small want. Whole crowds are made of it.
lhand: a wound kept open so it can be shown
Your hurt held out in the open hand. Faiths have been built on less. Faiths have been built on exactly this.
a good place near the front, to see
Your spot at every killing, kept. Not cruel. Curious. Curiosity is how the Maiden fills her crowds.
rhand: your tears, to whoever will gather them
You give your grief away and someone bottles it. Somewhere a relic will be made of what you wept. Not a pleasant thought, is it.
the girl in the iron, to her weeping
You turn away from the one suffering and let her go on. Everyone did. Look how that turned out.
belly: bleeding for nothing in an empty square
Suffering with no one to see. Pain without a witness is only pain. You want yours to be a sermon.
being the one they come to watch
The iron, and the crowd turning to look. You're right to be afraid. The crowd is always looking for its next saint.
feet: a procession road, still wet
You came behind the penitents, stepping where they bled. That road ends at a wall. They all go into the wall. Everyone behind moves up.
the road the crowd takes home, after
The way the onlookers go, talking low, not looking back. That road leads home, and home leads back to the square.
under: a suffering that made a faith
Under you, an old agony, still being believed. Every belief here needs a body. Hers is spoken for. They'll be looking for another.
a crowd of faces that did nothing
Under everything, the watchers, shoulder to shoulder. They watched the Maiden made. They're watching now. Wave, if you like.

turned.head: Turn the Saint over and you get the crowd. All those faces, none of them weeping. Look closer. ...See yourself?
turned.hands: Not her, then. The watchers, hands tucked in their sleeves. The Weeping Saint, the wrong way up.
turned.low: Head down, she gives the crowd's view of the iron. Everyone gets a good view from down there.

mantles.one: the one who reads until it is read

brow: a reader's squint, gone glassy from the page
A face that has stopped looking at people and started reading them. They'll feel it. They'll tell you things they meant to keep.
a face the Needle has already seen
Something far off has taken this face's measure. You'll be known in places you've never been. Mind the eyes on high walls.
heart: to know, whatever knowing costs
You'll pay. The knowing kind always do. The first price is always small. That's how the reading rooms filled up.
to be unseen again
To be shut, a book back on the shelf. Too late. A thing once read stays read.
lhand: a book you can't stop reading
The page turns itself under your thumb. Somewhere near the end is a chapter about you, one page ahead. Don't skip.
an eye that won't close
The watching, carried everywhere, never put down to sleep. The Citadel's readers had a word for it, before they stopped sleeping at all.
rhand: everything you read, once you knew it
You let the learning go and keep only the knowing. Lighter. Colder. A scholar who forgets the books becomes something else.
the page that started reading back
You drop the book. Too late. It has your scent. Somewhere a page is still turned toward you.
belly: a page with nothing left to teach you
An end to learning. A funny fear, here. The Hide has plenty left to teach, and none of it kindly.
the eyes in the Needle, turning your way
You fear being read more than dying. That's the right order, here.
feet: the long stair up to the reading rooms
Up from the stacks, ink on your soles. The Citadel's oldest reader looked up the day you passed, they say. Then looked down again.
a road the Needle watched you walk
Every step under an eye. The Needle doesn't follow. It doesn't need to. It has read how the road ends.
under: the oldest reader, asleep over his book
Under everything, a reader who hasn't turned a page in an age. The book is open at you. Don't wake him. He'll want to know how it ends.
something reading you, line by line
Under you something reads, and you're the page. Every step written as it's taken. Every word read as it's written.

turned.head: Ah. Now the Eye is reading you. Don't blink. It notes the blinking.
turned.hands: That one's turned to look back up your arm. The Scholar's Eye, upside down. Something in the Needle has the page open.
turned.low: Watching from underneath, the Eye. Low on the body, and very patient. An old habit of the Needle's.

mantles.one: the one a breath behind

brow: a face that hangs head down in every pool
You've a twin in every still water, and the twin's face is the true one. People will feel they've met you before. They have. Upside down.
the face of the one waiting up ahead
You wear the twin's face, the one that went first. Some will greet you by a name you don't know. Answer to it. See what happens.
heart: to catch your other half
Always a breath behind something that looks just like you. The chasing will be your whole life. The catching would end it.
never to be caught
To stay a breath ahead of what follows. You'll run well. Running is a kind of faith.
lhand: the rope you were hung by, still knotted
You keep the knot that held you. Not as a warning. As a handhold. There's a difference, and it's thin.
a hand reaching back out of still water
You're holding a hand nobody else can see. The water's very cold. You won't let go.
rhand: your reflection, for one breath
You let your twin go, a breath, and for that breath you're alone the way nothing here has been alone. Then the water stills.
the breath you were ahead by
You give up your lead and the one behind closes the gap. Whatever happens when you meet was always going to.
belly: still water
The mirror that doesn't ripple, and the thing in it that doesn't blink. Keep away from the black glass, then. ...Ah. Never mind.
the moment the twin stops waiting
The other turning round. What looks back out of water has been patient so long. Patience ends.
feet: the shore of every still pool
Along the water's edge, keeping pace with your reflection. Look at the footprints. Two sets. One of them goes in.
a road the other one walked first
Every step already taken, a breath ago, by the same feet. You're following yourself. You don't know it yet.
under: the Drowned Twin, keeping very good time
Under you, face up in the Red, the twin. Lift a hand. ...There. It lifted one too. A breath late.
a twin a step ahead, who knows the way
The one under the Red is a breath ahead. It knows where you're going. It's already there, waiting, wet.

turned.head: The Twin, right way up for once. Which means reversed. The one in the water is the true one, you see.
turned.hands: A breath ahead now, the Hanged Twin. It already knows which you'll choose.
turned.low: Ha. Hangs upright when it's reversed, that one. Waiting at the bottom, a breath ahead of you.

mantles.one: the one that eats to keep

brow: a mouth, and behind it another mouth
A face that smiles with more than one smile. People will feel hollow around you and not know why.
a face with bite marks in it
Something has had a taste of this face already, and means to come back. They'll see the marks and stand a little further off.
heart: to swallow, and keep what you swallow
A hunger that isn't for anything. It's for keeping. Every hunger here is a hunger to keep. The old one kept everything, once.
to be swallowed, and be done
To be taken in and stop being separate. It sounds like rest. It's a throat.
lhand: a hunger fed with both hands
You keep the appetite itself, not the thing it wants. You can't fill a hand that's holding a hunger.
a bone with your own teeth marks in it
Gnawing on yourself when there's nothing else. Keeps the wanting sharp. Keeps it lean.
rhand: the scraps, never the whole
You give away what you don't want and call it charity. The Knot is generous like that. The mouths keep the rest.
the last of yourself, to the mouths
You let yourself be taken. A little. Then more. The mouths are very good at a little, then more.
belly: an empty belly
The hollow, more than any blade. Empty is where you started. You'll fill yourself with anything to keep from going back.
the Second Mouth, preaching
The voice that says hunger is holy. You fear it because you've heard the sermon, and found it beautiful.
feet: a road with a mouth at both ends
Out of one mouth, toward the other. That's a throat, not a road. Most roads here are.
a road that goes round and down
Spiralling, every turn a little lower. You think you're walking. You're being swallowed slowly. Same thing, from inside.
under: one hunger with many mouths
Under you the Knot, working quietly. Everything goes down into the Red sooner or later. The Red is a mouth too.
what the Tallow-Mother keeps for later
Under everything, something set aside, wrapped in fat and patience. Kept. For later. Whose later, I couldn't tell you.

turned.head: Turned, and the mouths are on the outside now. That's the side that gets swallowed.
turned.hands: Seen from inside one of the mouths. That's the Knot, inverted. Damp in there.
turned.low: In the belly, head down, the Knot of Mouths. It'll gnaw from below. Patient little teeth.

mantles.one: the one that burns down to give light
mantles.rev: the dark at the edge of the light

brow: a face lit from below by its own burning
You'll look like you're carrying a light, and you are. The light is you. Those beside you will be warm, and won't ask what's burning.
a face just past where the light reaches
The face at the edge of the lantern, half there. People will think you're following them. Sometimes they'll be right.
heart: to burn down for a little light
Spending yourself, gladly. The lanterns are full of hearts like that. That isn't a comfort. That's what's in the lanterns.
the dark that waits for every flame
You want the after, when the burning's done. A heart like that is patient with everyone, and everyone should be afraid of it.
lhand: a lantern with a soul inside it
You carry someone's burning to see by. Whose? Lanterns don't say. They flicker when you ask.
a cold wick, burned all the way down
What's left when the light is spent, and you won't throw it away. Mourning, or thrift. Hard to tell which, here.
rhand: the last of your tallow, to the light
You give your last to keep a flame alive. That's how the lantern bearers end, mostly. In a lantern, giving light to strangers.
the light, a step at a time
You let the light go and follow the dark at its edge. Easier on the eyes. Harder on everything else.
belly: going out
The flame's own fear, the little gutter at the end. You'll start at every draught, and stand near the Red and shiver.
the light finding you
Being seen. The edge of the dark was always safe. Lanterns change that. Lanterns are coming.
feet: a road lit one lantern at a time
Somebody lit the way for you, flame by flame, and every flame was somebody. You walked on all of them, lit.
the dark verge just off the lantern road
Beside the light, never in it. The roadside has its own travellers. They keep to the edges for good reason.
under: a soul that stayed to burn
Under you, someone chose to stay and be the light. Still burning, down in the Red, for your sake. Be worth it.
the patient dark the light only pushes back a step
Under everything, the dark the lanterns lean against. It doesn't push. It doesn't need to. It has waited out every flame so far.

turned.head: The dark at the edge of the flame, looking in at you. That's the Wick turned round.
turned.hands: Wick down, the dark leaning in. It's very patient, that dark. It has outlasted every flame so far.
turned.low: Burning downward, into the Red. The Wick never comes out of that well.

mantles.one: the one who cuts her hair

brow: a shorn head bowed toward the Red
Grief worn plain and cut close. People will tell you their dead without being asked. You'll carry a great many names that way, and none of them yours.
the face someone is still weeping over
Somebody wept over this face before you rose in it. You look like someone. You'll meet people who stop dead at the sight of you.
heart: grief that cuts, and keeps cutting
Loving the cutting more than what was lost. Every mourning makes the next one easier. That's the horror of it.
to be remembered by someone
To have someone cut their hair for you. A simple want. The hardest thing on the Hide to come by, with so few left to cut.
lhand: a lock of cut hair
A lock of someone. You won't say who. Every morning you'll check it's still there. Every mourning, I should say.
a name somebody else is grieving
A stranger's grief, carried by mistake and folded small. It'll steer you. Grief makes a better compass than most.
rhand: everyone the Red takes
You let them go to the water without a fight. The Grandmother does the same. One day it'll be you on the shore with the scissors.
the one who mourns you, unknowing
Somewhere someone grieves for you, and you let them, and walk the other way. Kind, or cowardly. Grief doesn't care which.
belly: the sound of the scissors at the tide line
The next loss, because there's always a next. You'll hear the blades in the surf. Everyone on this shore does, at night.
being forgotten by the one who grieved
The worst fear on the shore. To be mourned, and then not. To be cut away with the hair.
feet: the tide line, walked at dusk
Along the wrack and the drowned, the way the mourners walk. The Red came up to meet you. It does that, for its own.
a funeral road, walked the wrong way
From the grave toward the living, against the procession. They stepped aside for you and didn't know why.
under: the Grandmother of the Red, with no hair left to cut
Under you, the oldest mourning of all, shorn bare and still weeping. She's grieving for you already. Ahead of time. She's always ahead of time.
your own wake, held long before you rose
Under everything, a mourning for you, finished and swept up. Rather a lot of hair, for someone only just born.

turned.head: Someone's mourning you already. That's what the Mourner means, head down. That was quick.
turned.hands: The grieved-for, not the griever. Cut hair everywhere, and your name in all of it.
turned.low: A wake, held down at your feet. The Mourner reversed. Short notice, but well attended.

mantles.one: the one who locks the count

brow: an iron face with the count behind it
A face like a locked door. People will think something precious is inside. Something is. Not what they'd hope.
the face of whoever comes with the key
A face that opens things. Doors will. People won't, around you. They'll hold their breath and hope you pass.
heart: every bone in its place
Order to the last splinter. Beyond the Pale they'd call that holy. Out here it's merely exhausting.
the door the Pale Order keeps shut
To open the one thing that should stay closed. Every keeper has that want, deep down. That's why they're chosen. They know it from inside.
lhand: a key that locks the count
The closing, in your hand. Nothing gets out past you. Nothing gets in either, and that's lonelier than it sounds.
a key never meant to be turned
Warm from waiting. Something on the far side of the lock knows exactly whose hand it's in.
rhand: whatever you locked away
You let go of what you shut in, and forget where the door was. Mercy, perhaps. The door won't forget.
the lock, and all it kept
You let the count go. Bones out of their places, rattling in the dark. Somewhere beyond the Pale a brother wakes and can't say why.
belly: a bone out of its place
One splinter wrong and you can't sleep. Every keeper is a little mad that way. You'll count the fallen under your breath, and hate yourself for it.
the click of the lock giving way
Listening for it, always. Every door that shuts behind you, you'll turn to check. One day you'll hear it.
feet: the cloisters of the Pale, swept bare
The long cold halls where the count is kept. Bare feet on bare stone. You know the number of every flagstone and don't know you know it.
a road through a door left open
You came through a place that should have been locked, and wasn't. Someone left it ajar. Someone will be blamed.
under: the lock the whole world turns in
Under you the count, closed, and the world held shut by it. Heavy to lie on. Heavier to stand on, which is what you'll be doing.
a hand already on the key
Under everything, the turning has begun. Slowly. Hear it? No. You won't, until it's done.

turned.head: Somebody's opening the count. In the head, of all places. That's the Key, turned.
turned.hands: The lock's on the other side of the door now. Ossuary Key, reversed. Which side are you on?
turned.low: Turning, low down. Down there the Key opens what was shut for good reason.

mantles.one: the one who asks at the door

brow: a beggar's face at the door, very polite
Humble, patient, harmless to look at. That's the face the Ghauul wears too, when it knocks.
the face that opens the door at night
A house that answers. Welcoming. Too welcoming. People will stay too long near you and wake lighter.
heart: marrow, asked for nicely
What's at the middle of things, and you'll ask, and ask, and ask. Politeness is a kind of siege.
to let the knocking in
To open the door just to see. There are more doors here than there are living to open them.
lhand: an empty bowl held out
Need itself, held out. Strangers will drop things in. Some of those things will still be moving.
a latch you have already lifted
You're holding the door open a crack. You think nobody's noticed. Something has.
rhand: your pride, for asking at all
You drop the pride and keep the bowl. Beggars last. The proud are mostly bones in the heaps below the stair.
the door, wide open
You let go of the door and the night walks in. Guest, or tenant, or owner. You find out which by morning.
belly: the door staying shut
The knock nobody answers. Asking forever. That's the Ghauul's fear too, if it fears. Odd company to keep.
whatever is knocking
The asking at the door. You'll hear it everywhere. Hollow trees, old helms, your own ribs.
feet: a road from door to door to door
The long way, asking at every house. The houses are all empty now. You asked anyway. Something answered at the last one.
a road that ends at your own threshold
All the way round, back to your own door, knocking. Let yourself in? Careful. It doesn't look quite like you.
under: the Ghauul, knocking for marrow
Under you, the polite one, knuckles to the floor of the world. Knock, knock. It will knock all your life, waiting for you to answer.
a house that answered once
Under everything, a door already opened. Whatever came in through it is still inside. You're standing on its roof.

turned.head: The house that answers. You've opened the door, haven't you. In your sleep. That's the Cup the wrong way up.
turned.hands: Empty bowl, open door. Knock, knock. The Beggar's Cup, inverted.
turned.low: Spilled, the Cup. Low down the door's a cellar door. Don't open it. You will.

mantles.one: the one who rings under the water

brow: a face that hears something under the water
Always listening for a sound nobody else catches. You'll stop mid-step, head tilted. Others will stop too, hear nothing, and be afraid.
a face that rings true, and shouldn't
Everything you say will sound right. Clear as a bell. On the Hide nothing true is clear, so mind what sounds it.
heart: to answer a call only the drowned can hear
Something under the water is calling, and you want to answer. That's a long way down from wanting to live.
to ring one true note, once
One clear sound in a broken world. Ambitious. The drowned court would come up to hear it. All of them.
lhand: a clapper wrapped in weed
The bell's silence, the muffle, held in your hand. While you hold it the court stays down. Your hand will cramp.
a note held perfectly in tune
Something exact. Exact things draw attention. Down in the water, something keeps time with you.
rhand: the living, out of step
You let go the warm and the clumsy and fall into the drowned court's time. Graceful, after that. Very graceful. Very cold.
the long quiet the bell kept
You let it go, and the bell rings. Somewhere under the water a court begins to walk.
belly: the bell stopping
The silence after the last ring. The drowned keep time by that bell. If it stops, they'll come up to see why.
the bell sounding right
Perfect pitch. A sound with no flaw in it. Somehow you know the world wasn't built to bear one.
feet: the old spine, walked in step with the drowned
Along the bones of something huge, keeping time with feet that weren't there. You'll walk in step with them a while yet. Count the beat.
a road that rings under every footfall
Every step sounded, all the way here, and every step was heard. Hollow ground. Something under it was listening.
under: the drowned king's court, walking
Under you, a procession in the Red, in perfect step, going somewhere it never arrives. It's walking toward you now. Slowly. Always slowly.
a drowned bell, in tune at last
Under everything, the bell has found its note. Can you hear it? Lucky. The drowned can, and they're all turning to listen.

turned.head: Ringing true, and upside down. A drowned bell in tune. That's the frightening one.
turned.hands: Mouth up, the Bell, full of the Red. One clean note out of it and they'll all come up to listen.
turned.low: Rung in tune, under you. Feel it in your heels? No. You will.

mantles.one: the one who sells at the end of the world

brow: a merchant's smile on a picked-clean face
A face that prices things. People will feel weighed when you look at them. Some will like it, the way the drowning like a rope.
the face of a buyer who didn't ask the price
Eager. Open. Easy to sell to. You'll leave most bargains a little poorer and not mind. The minding comes later.
heart: to sell whatever is left
Everything has a price at the end of the world, even the end of the world. You want to know what it would fetch.
to buy, and pay too much
To own something, anything, at any cost, on a dead shore, from the one merchant left. Think what he charges.
lhand: a coin from the end of the world
The first coin, or the last. Same coin. It'll buy one thing, once. Choose carefully. Or don't. The coin chooses anyway.
a thing you paid far too much for
The bargain kept close, and you won't say what it cost. You'll find out. Everyone finds out what things cost, here.
rhand: whatever will sell
Anything with a price, you let go. Nothing you own will last. You'll be light, and empty, and never quite poor.
the price, gladly
You pay without counting. Generous, or careless. The merchant loves that kind. He'll remember you.
belly: having nothing left to sell
The merchant's fear, and it's catching. When there's nothing left, they say, you sell the name. You haven't got one yet. You'll want one, for that.
what you have already paid
The bill. It's been settled, and you don't know what with. Something's missing. Count your fingers. Count your names.
feet: the market road along the dead shore
The merchant's way, past every corpse he'd picked. Some of them still had their coin. Not anymore.
a road you bought, and paid for twice
Every step of it purchased. The seller's still owed. He'll come along the shore one day with his hand out, smiling.
under: the merchant who picks the shore clean
Under you, the last trader, counting. He's priced you already. Not a high price. He's very fair.
a bargain struck in the dark, still open
Under everything, a deal half done. Somebody sold you into the world. The buyer hasn't come to collect. Yet.

turned.head: Not the seller now. The buyer. And you haven't even asked the price.
turned.hands: The First Coin, face down in your palm. You're the one paying. Turn out your pockets... ah. No pockets yet.
turned.low: Paid for already, whatever it was. That's the Coin, low and inverted. Paid low.

mantles.one: the one that hardens what is given to it

brow: a face fired hard
Whatever was soft in it went into the heat and didn't come out. People will break against you. You won't notice.
a face with a crack across it
Fired too fast. It'll hold, mostly, but light comes through the crack at angles, and people will stare at the light.
heart: to be hardened by what you go through
You want the fire. You want to come out iron. The Deep sets the old one's blood that way, slow, under the world. It's a long firing.
to break in the fire and be done
To shatter rather than set. Iron lasts. Shards rest.
lhand: a coal you won't drop
Heat in a bare hand. That hand won't be soft again. That hand will be very good at holding.
a shard that broke in the firing
The failure, sharp, carried close, and you keep cutting yourself on it. You'll know the shape of the break better than the shape of the pot.
rhand: everything soft in you
You let it go piece by piece. Kindness first, usually. Then the rest. The fire is very thorough.
the shape you were meant to have
The mould let go before it set. Now you're whatever shape the fire left. Ugly, maybe. Your own.
belly: going in soft and coming out soft
That nothing will change you. That you'll go through everything and be no harder. You'll go looking for heat.
the crack you can feel spreading
What's already happening. A fine line through the middle. Listen at night. You'll hear it tick.
feet: a road through the heat under everything
Up from below, past the Deep, where the blood turns to iron. Your feet were warm when you rose. Did you notice? I did.
a road of broken pots
Shards the whole way. Everything that came out of the fire wrong was thrown on that road. You walked out over the failures. You're not one of them. Yet.
under: the Deep, setting blood to iron in the dark
Under you, the slow forge of the world, patient as a mother. Every iron thing on the Hide came from there. You'll feel at home near iron.
a crack running all the way down
Under everything, a fault. The whole world was fired with a flaw in it, and you're standing right on the line. Tread lightly.

turned.head: Something cracked in the firing. Up near the face, too. The Kiln, reversed.
turned.hands: A shard, not a pot. That's how the Kiln lies turned over. Sharp, though. Very sharp.
turned.low: A crack running downward. Cracks always find the bottom. The Kiln knows.

mantles.one: the one who unpicks

brow: a face coming undone, thread by thread
Something is unpicking this face, and humming. People will see it fray and pity you. Pity is a thread too. The Crone picks that one out last.
a face stitched back together, lumpy
Mended badly, but mended. People will see the stitches and trust you more, oddly. Mended things have been through something.
heart: to be unpicked down to the first thread
To know what you were before the weaving. There's nothing there. The first thread is tied to nothing. That's the trick of it.
to be stitched back together, however badly
To be whole, even ugly. A sound want. The Crone won't allow it. That's what makes it brave.
lhand: a loose thread you keep pulling
You can't leave it alone. Every tug undoes a little more. Of what? Pull and find out, you'll say.
a knot of thread from somebody else's life
A tangle that isn't yours. Some other weaving got caught on you. You'll find its owner, or what's left. The thread will see to it.
rhand: whatever was woven wrong
You let the mistakes unravel. Cleaner, after. Thinner too. A cloth can only lose so many threads.
a thread you should have kept
You let go of something that held you together. You won't notice until the wind gets in.
belly: the humming behind the veil
The Crone's tune. You'll hear it in the wind, in wet sand dragging back, in your own breath. A low tune. Patient fingers.
unravelling all at once
Not slowly. One pulled thread and the whole thing in a heap. You'll walk very carefully, as if that could help.
feet: a road that unspools behind you
Every step, the road behind comes undone. No going back. There never was. Now you're only honest about it.
a road darned from other people's roads
Patched from journeys past counting, none of them yours. You'll know places you've never been. Don't trust that knowing.
under: the Crone, picking you out and humming
Under you, the one behind the veil, already at work, fingers in the weave. She has found your loose end. She's in no hurry.
a patch that holds, mostly
Under everything, a repair, crude, holding the whole spread together. Somebody mended this world once. Rather badly. It's held so far.

turned.head: Reweaving. Lumpy work. Somebody is mending your face and isn't very good at it.
turned.hands: Stitching instead of picking, the Loom inverted. A clumsy needle, but a stubborn one.
turned.low: Darned at the bottom. Patches hold, low down. It's the hems that go first.

mantles.one: the one who keeps what is lost
mantles.rev: the one who lets it go

brow: a maker's soot-dark face
The face of someone who makes the lights. Nobody does, now. People will see it and remember there used to be such hands. So will the ones who hunted them.
a face that looks up as the light goes out
Watching the kept soul leave the lantern like a breath. A face for farewells. You'll be good at them. You'll have many.
heart: to keep what was lost
You can't bear the going. You'll hold the dead in glass and flame. That's love, here. It's also a cage.
to let go of everything you kept
To open every lantern. A beautiful want, and a terrible one. The kept are all that's lighting the way.
lhand: a lantern nobody knows how to make anymore
The last of a craft, in your hand. People will want it. People will kill for it. People have.
an empty lantern with its door open
The lantern after the breath has left it. Empty, and still warm. You won't say who was inside.
rhand: anything you try to keep
Everything you hold, you'll lose, and you know it. You'll make the light anyway. That's what makers are for.
a breath, out of the top of the lantern
You let the kept one go. The light rises like an out-breath and is gone. The road gets darker. The soul gets free. Pick one.
belly: the last lantern going dark
The world unlit. Fair enough. It's mostly unlit already. You'll carry your light through it like a held breath.
being kept, when you want to go
The glass. Ending up inside, shining for strangers. Every lantern carries you back when you fall. Think on that.
feet: the road the hunted makers took
Quiet, at night, without lights. The makers learned to walk dark. They had their reasons.
a road that goes up and out with the light
You came down the way the freed go up. Against the current. Something has noticed you came down.
under: the last maker, hiding something lit
Under you, someone crouched over a little flame, shielding it. The last of the makers. What they're keeping alive down there is no business of mine. Or yours. Yet.
every soul let out of every lantern
Under everything, all the freed lights, gone up and out. Nothing left to see by. You'll make do with what you carry.

turned.head: The lantern's door is open. Someone's breath, going up and out of the top. The Wright, reversed.
turned.hands: Letting go of the kept. Brave hands, those. Cold, after.
turned.low: The light is leaving by the top, and you're down at the bottom with the Lantern-Wright on its head.

mantles.one: the one who holds the note

brow: a mouth open on a note that never ends
Always about to speak, always singing something under it. People will lean close to hear. Don't let them lean too close.
a face holding its breath
Tight, held, waiting. A face like that is a pause, and things come in through pauses. I'd keep talking, if I were you.
heart: to hold on, past all breath
To keep the note going when the lungs say no. Admirable. The Choir has held it for ages beyond counting, and look at them.
the rest between the notes
The gap where nothing is said. Once, everyone breathed in at the same moment. I won't tell you what came in.
lhand: a note you won't let go of
One sound, steady, against everything. That's how a world is kept up, they say. Someone always holding the note.
a breath you've been saving
Hoarded air, for something. A last word, or a first one. You'll know when. You won't like it.
rhand: your own voice, into the stone
You give your voice to the crypts. The walls will hum with it after you've gone. You'll go quieter all your life.
the note, at last
You let the note go. Just for a breath. In that breath something very large can slip in. It has before.
belly: the note ending
The last breath of the song, and what comes in after. A good instinct. Keep it.
what comes in the quiet
Not the dark. Not the dead. The gap between words. The oldest fear there is, and truer than the rest.
feet: the low wet roads under the crypts
Up through the Choir's own passages, and the note followed you up the stair. Put an ear to your bones and you can hear it still.
a road with no sound on it at all
Not a footfall, not a breath, the whole way. You came out of a quiet so deep it had no name. Let's not give it one.
under: the Drowned Choir, still holding the note
Under you, the long note, rising out of the Red. It's what keeps the floor up, more or less. Don't interrupt them.
the rest the singers are afraid of
Under everything, a gap in the song. Something lives in it. It's been very patient. It has nothing else to be.

turned.head: The rest between the notes. ...Hear it? No. That's the point. That's the whole point.
turned.hands: Mouths shut, the Drowned Choir. A breath between notes. Don't fill it.
turned.low: Low on you, the Choir turned over. The gap under the song. Something lives in the gap.

mantles.one: the one who owes
mantles.rev: the one who comes to collect

brow: a debtor's lowered face
The face of the Tithed, all of them, eyes down. You'll pass among the last of them and be taken for kin. You might be.
a polite face at the door at night
The collector's face. Unhurried. Owed. People will pay you things before you ask. That's the face working.
heart: to be paid up, and free
To owe nothing. Nobody here has ever owed nothing. The want will drive you hard, and the debt will grow faster than the paying.
everything, not just your share
To collect it all, every debt the world owes. That's a great deal of knocking. You'll have the patience. Collectors do.
lhand: a debt nobody remembers taking
The owing, kept close, like a stone in a pocket. Whose loan? Nobody remembers. Everybody pays. That's the Tithe.
a ledger with your own name in it
You keep the book. Your name's in it, near the bottom, unpaid. Funny. You haven't got a name yet. The ledger has.
rhand: your share, every time
You pay without arguing. A good debtor. The best debtors are bled the longest. Everything here takes its share of the hide.
the waiting, to go and collect
You stop waiting to be paid and go knocking in person. Doors will open faster after that. Not gladly.
belly: the knock
The collector's knock, at the dark end of the night. The Tithed all fear it. You'll lie awake listening, hear your own heart, and think it's the door.
a debtor who cannot pay
The one who owes and has nothing. What does a collector take then? You know. That's the fear.
feet: a road paved with what was paid
Over the offerings of everyone who paid before. A road of small losses, smooth with walking. Every stone a little piece of someone.
the collector's road, walked at night
The way the collector comes. Doors shut along that road as you passed. They knew the step.
under: a loan from whatever gave the first mourning
Under you, the first debt, older than anyone. You were born owing. So were we all. Don't feel special.
the one who comes to collect
Under everything, the collector, by the door of the world. Not for you. Not yet. Only checking the address.

turned.head: The collector, not the debtor. Polite. Punctual. That's the Tithe from the other side.
turned.hands: Your hand out, and someone else's pockets. How the Tithe turns.
turned.low: The collector's down in the cellar. Been there a while, by the look of the card.

mantles.one: the one whose orders are never obeyed
mantles.rev: the city that would obey if it could
mantles.wears: the Man in the Rust, on the dark moon

brow: a hollow crown, giving orders to the wind
A face that commands, and nothing listens. The wind is very polite about it. You'll keep giving orders. A habit. Also a curse.
a face waiting to be told what to do
An obedient face, ready. People will try to use it. Something on the brown moon will try too. It is always looking for willing faces.
heart: to be obeyed, just once
One order followed. That's all. The Man in the Rust has wanted the same since before the world had a name. It's a lonely want.
to obey, with nothing left to obey
To kneel to something and find it has no hands. The Hide is full of people who want this. They make the best faithful.
lhand: an order no one will carry out
A command held like a coal. You can't pass it on. You can't drop it. It'll burn there until someone takes it, and nobody will.
the keys of an empty city
Every door of a place no one lives. Streets of rust. You'll know the way through them in your sleep. You'll go there in your sleep.
rhand: the crown, though it never fit
You set down a rule you never had. Easier, after. A crown that fits nobody is lighter on the ground.
your last order, into the silence
You give the final command and let it go out into nothing. Nothing answers. That's an answer, here.
belly: nobody listening
That you're speaking to no one. That the cards are. That I am. ...Well. Moving on.
an order you can't refuse
Being told. Being bound. Something on the dark moon has been composing an order for a very long time. It will fit you exactly.
feet: a road toward the brown moon
You came up out of the Red already facing the dark moon. Not walking toward it. Facing it. Turn your head away now and then. Do.
the empty streets of the city that would obey
Through rust and doorways, and every doorway leaned toward you, wanting an order. You gave none. They're still leaning.
under: the Man in the Rust, still giving orders
Under you, in the Red, the dark moon's reflection, and in it the Man in the Rust, commanding. Reflections listen better than people do. That's what worries me.
an empty city, waiting for a voice
Under everything, rust and doorways, all waiting to be told. One day you'll speak near them. Mind what you say.

turned.head: A city kneeling with nobody to kneel to. The Hollow Crown, upside down.
turned.hands: Worn on the wrong end, that Crown. Obedience, with nothing left to obey.
turned.low: Rust running down into the Red. The empty city sits under everything, and it's listening for orders.
